Estimation engines for the Hierarchical Bayes models

Source: R/engine.R
hb_engine.Rd

Constructors for the engine argument of hb_area, hb_unit and hb_twofold. Each collects the settings of one estimation engine, so that the model functions themselves only describe the model. Passing the string "inla" or "jax" is the same as passing inla_engine() or jax_engine() with their defaults.

Usage

inla_engine(
  strategy = c("laplace", "simplified.laplace", "gaussian"),
  link = NULL,
  scale_model = TRUE,
  prior_prec = NULL,
  prior_phi = NULL,
  prior_rho = NULL,
  prior_prec_time = NULL,
  prior_rho_time = NULL,
  prior_prec_subarea = NULL,
  draws = NULL,
  seed = 1L,
  ...
)

jax_engine(
  warmup = 500,
  samples = 1000,
  chains = 2,
  device = c("auto", "cpu", "cuda", "metal"),
  seed = 42,
  prior_beta = c("normal", "horseshoe"),
  priors = c("inla", "weakly_informative"),
  robust = FALSE,
  keep_draws = TRUE,
  progress = interactive()
)

# S3 method for class 'fastsae_engine'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

strategy

INLA approximation strategy: "laplace" (default, full Laplace approximation, highest accuracy), "simplified.laplace" (faster) or "gaussian" (fastest).

link

Link function for the likelihood (hb_area() only). NULL (default) uses the canonical link of the family: identity for gaussian, logit for binomial and beta, log for poisson, nbinomial and gamma. Binomial and beta also accept "probit", "cloglog" and "loglog". The estimates (hb) are on the response scale for any link.

scale_model

Logical; scale the intrinsic GMRF models (besag, bym, rw1, rw2) to a generalized variance of 1. Default TRUE.

prior_prec

Prior for the precision of the area (domain) random effect. NULL (default), in all HB functions: a half-normal prior on the standard deviation (given to INLA as an "expression:" prior), with scale \(s_y\), the standard deviation of the observed responses, for family = "gaussian" and scale 1 on the link scale (logit, log) of the other families. An area standard deviation cannot exceed \(s_y\), so the Gaussian prior only sets the scale and does not depend on the unit of the response. INLA's PC prior list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)) does: on mys with the response in tenths it moved the estimates by up to 4.1 posterior SD. In simulations the 95% intervals covered 93-97% of the true values with the half-normal prior against 85-92% with that PC prior (Fay-Herriot, 15-60 areas; EBLUP: 93-96%), and 93-95% against 92-94% for binomial and beta responses, where the PC prior also underestimated the area SD by up to 18%.

prior_phi

Prior for the mixing parameter of spatial = "bym2". NULL (default): the PC prior list(prior = "pc", param = c(0.5, 0.5)).

prior_rho

Prior for the spatial correlation of spatial = "generic1" or "slm" (hb_area() only); NULL uses the INLA default.

prior_prec_time

Prior for the precision of the temporal random effect (hb_area() only); NULL: the default of prior_prec.

prior_rho_time

Prior for the autocorrelation of temporal = "ar1" (hb_area() only); NULL uses the INLA default.

prior_prec_subarea

Prior for the precision of the subarea random effect (hb_twofold() only). NULL: the default of prior_prec.

draws

Number of posterior draws: from INLA::inla.posterior.sample() for posterior self-benchmarking in hb_area() (NULL: 1000), and for the area aggregates of the binomial and Poisson hb_twofold() models (NULL: 2000; 0 skips the sampling and approximates the aggregate uncertainty from independent sub-area effects). hb_twofold() draws them in R from the Gaussian approximation of the latent field at each of INLA's hyperparameter configurations, without INLA's skewness correction (which changed the aggregates less than the Monte Carlo error of 20000 draws), in well under a second instead of 0.3 s per configuration. The Gaussian aggregates are exact INLA linear combinations and need no draws.

seed

Random seed of the sampler. Default 42.

...

Further arguments passed to INLA::inla(), such as control.compute or num.threads.

warmup

Number of warmup (adaptation) iterations per chain. Default 500.

samples

Number of posterior draws kept per chain. Default 1000.

chains

Number of MCMC chains. Default 2; 4 is recommended for checking convergence. With more than one chain, the fit reports the largest rank-normalized split R-hat and convergence is rhat_max < 1.05 (see the section MCMC convergence).

device

"auto" (default: CUDA when available, otherwise CPU), "cpu", "cuda" or "metal" (Apple silicon GPU, through jax-metal). JAX fixes its device at the first fit of an R session. "metal" has a fixed cost of about two minutes per fit, so on Apple silicon it pays off only for large numbers of domains (thousands); for that reason "auto" uses the CPU on macOS.

prior_beta

Prior for the regression coefficients: "normal" (default) or "horseshoe" (regularized horseshoe, for many candidate covariates).

priors

Default priors of the model parameters. "inla" (default): the defaults of inla_engine(), so that both engines fit the same model: every random-effect standard deviation gets the default of inla_engine(prior_prec = ) (half-normal with scale \(s_y\) for Gaussian models, 1 on the link scale otherwise), the BYM2 mixing parameter \(\phi\) INLA's PC prior (\(P(\phi < 0.5) = 0.5\)), the AR(1) correlation INLA's \(N(0, 1/0.15)\) prior on \(\log((1 + \rho)/(1 - \rho))\), the Leroux and SAR correlations uniform priors, and the coefficients \(N(0, 1000)\). On mys the two engines then agree within 0.03 (iid) and 0.05 (BYM2) posterior SD. "weakly_informative": half-normal standard deviations with scale 1 on the standardised response or the link scale, uniform \(\phi\) and AR(1) correlation and \(N(0, 10^2)\) coefficients (\(N(0, 2.5^2)\) for logit links). The priors of the likelihood are the same as with inla_engine(): half-normal(\(s_y\)) on the Gaussian residual SD without vardir (and on the unit errors of hb_unit()), half-normal(10) on the negative binomial size and the gamma shape, and INLA's log-gamma(1, 0.1) on the log beta precision (\(\phi \sim\) Exponential(0.1)); "weakly_informative" keeps half-normal(10) for the beta precision.

robust

Logical; Student-t instead of normal random effects (the area effects, and the sub-area effects of hb_twofold()), with the degrees of freedom estimated. Default FALSE.

keep_draws

Logical; keep the posterior draws of the area parameters in $draws of the fit (needed by benchmark_sae() to propagate the posterior covariance). Default TRUE.

progress

Logical; show NumPyro's progress bar. Default interactive().

x

A "fastsae_engine" object.

Value

An object of class "fastsae_engine".

INLA

inla_engine() fits the model by integrated nested Laplace approximation (INLA); it is available for all HB models. Priors are given in INLA syntax. A prior or setting left at NULL takes the default of the model function; a setting the model does not use (such as prior_rho_time in hb_unit()) is ignored with a warning.

JAX

jax_engine() fits the model by MCMC (NumPyro's No-U-Turn sampler on JAX, Phan et al. 2019) on CPU, CUDA GPU or Apple Metal, through reticulate. It needs Python with jax and numpyro; see setup_numpyro_env (check_only = TRUE checks it). The fixed effects get a normal or a regularized horseshoe prior (Piironen and Vehtari 2017); see priors for the other priors. spatial = "slm" and temporal = "rw2" are not available. jax_engine() is available for hb_area(), hb_unit() and hb_twofold().

MCMC convergence

A jax_engine() fit carries the diagnostics of Vehtari et al. (2021), computed as the R package posterior does: mcmc_diagnostics, a table of the rank-normalized split R-hat and the bulk and tail effective sample sizes (ESS) of every hyperparameter (variances, phi, rho, ...), coefficient and area or domain parameter (hb[j], row j of df_hb); rhat_max and ess_min, their extremes; divergences, the number of divergent transitions after warmup; treedepth_hits, the iterations that reached the maximum tree depth; and trace, the per-chain draws (iterations x chains x parameters) of the hyperparameters, up to eight coefficients and the area with the largest R-hat. convergence is rhat_max < 1.05, as before. A fit warns when R-hat is at least 1.05, when the bulk or tail ESS is below 100 per chain or when there are divergent transitions (warning class fastsae_mcmc_warning), and informs when R-hat is between 1.01 and 1.05; Vehtari et al. recommend R-hat < 1.01 and ESS > 100 per chain. autoplot(fit, type = "trace") and type = "rank" plot the chains; see autoplot.fastsae.

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B., & Bürkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis, 16(2), 667-718.

References

Phan, D., Pradhan, N. and Jankowiak, M. (2019). Composable effects for flexible and accelerated probabilistic programming in NumPyro. arXiv:1912.11554.

Piironen, J. and Vehtari, A. (2017). Sparsity information and regularization in the horseshoe and other shrinkage priors. Electronic Journal of Statistics, 11(2), 5018–5051.

See also

hb_area, hb_unit, hb_twofold

Examples

inla_engine(strategy = "simplified.laplace")
#> INLA engine
#> • Strategy: simplified.laplace
#> • Link: canonical
jax_engine(samples = 2000, chains = 4, device = "cuda")
#> JAX engine (NumPyro NUTS)
#> • 4 chains x 2000 draws, 500 warmup, seed 42
#> • Device: cuda
#> • Prior on coefficients: normal
#> • Priors: inla
